components.gap: Not every claimed theorem of Barwise ch. A.1 is supplied with its exact hypotheses and a complete proof route; the following carry only missing-work records: (1) Keisler's Completeness Theorem and Compactness Theorem for L(Q) over a finite or countable language (Barwise pp. 44-45; owned body 1360-1367): no proof is written; Keisler 1970 is physically held at source/references/acq-r1-ACQ-2026-10-0225/ACQ-2026-10-0225.pdf (downloaded_verified), so the proof is writable in the owned body and annex. (2) The theory of groups is undecidable (Barwise p. 16; owned body 1652-1656): no proof is written; a complete route through a finitely presented group with unsolvable word problem is writable from the held Novikov1955 (source/references/acq-r1-ACQ-2026-10-0381/novikov-1955-word-problem.pdf) together with the reduction from the word problem to first-order consequence of the group axioms. (3) thm:p02-w02c-p02-003-integers-second (owned body 1607-1631) is proved only under the hypothesis that Prov_{T#} satisfies D2 and D3 and with an informal listing procedure; Barwise's p. 16 claim that the second incompleteness theorem shows how to find a true sentence of Z not implied by T is therefore supplied only conditionally (owned body 1657-1666); proofs of D2-D3 for the provability formula of the c.e. theory T# and a construction of its enumeration are owed. (4) Szmielew's theorem (abelian groups decidable, p. 16) and (5) the precise least-logic claim of p. 44 are blocked (see blocker).
